candidates.source_name: DKOM – Odločitve Državne revizijske komisije (decisions database)
candidates.why_relevant: Chronological, year-filterable list of every review decision of the national procurement review body. Each entry names the contracting authority in the URL slug and the decision number (018-XXX/YYYY); the decision text typically names the applicant/bidder, the disputed technical specifications and often prices. For banking/payments this is frequently the only public disclosure of who actually bid for payment-processing, card, cash-handling or bank-services contracts.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the year-filtered listing pages, harvest decision detail URLs (pattern /sl/revizijske-zadeve/odlocitve-dkom/<timestamp>/<018-nnn-yyyy>-<authority-slug>), extract decision text; incremental polling for new 018-*/2026 numbers.
queries_used: Državna revizijska komisija odločitve javna naročila bančne storitve
DKOM odločitev revizija javnega naročila bančne storitve

candidates.source_name: DKOM – Iskalnik po odločitvah (full-text decision search engine)
candidates.why_relevant: Keyword search across DKOM decisions – the practical entry point for topic-scoped retrieval such as 'bančne storitve', 'plačilni promet', 'POS terminali', 'kartično poslovanje'. Lets an analyst isolate the banking/payments subset out of ~thousands of decisions instead of crawling everything.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Query-driven harvesting with a Slovenian keyword list; capture result URLs and dedupe against the decisions listing crawl. Inspect query-string parameters before automating.
queries_used: DKOM prekrškovne zadeve odločbe o prekrških naročniki javna naročila objave

candidates.source_name: DKOM – Poročila o delu (annual work reports / review statistics)
candidates.why_relevant: Annual reports to the National Assembly containing statistics on review requests by procurement subject matter, outcomes (granted/partly granted/rejected), average resolution time and contracting-authority breakdowns. Gives the denominator for judging how contested a sector is, and flags trends in disputed sectors.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual PDF download + table extraction; watch the reports page each spring.
queries_used: DKOM letno poročilo o delu Državne revizijske komisije statistika zahtevkov za revizijo

candidates.source_name: DKOM – Prekrškovne zadeve (misdemeanour/infringement proceedings)
candidates.why_relevant: DKOM also acts as the misdemeanour authority against contracting authorities that breach procurement law. Infringement files reference the Public Procurement Portal publication number of the contract, linking a sanction to a specific tender – useful for spotting authorities that award banking/IT-payment contracts irregularly.
candidates.access_status: open web; degree of case-level publication unclear
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic page fetch; cross-reference any published sanction with eNaročanje publication numbers.
queries_used: DKOM prekrškovne zadeve odločbe o prekrških naročniki javna naročila objave

candidates.source_name: DKOM – National Review Commission (English pages)
candidates.why_relevant: English-language description of mandate, procedure and (some) reporting for the Slovenian review body; useful for cross-border comparison and for naming conventions in English-language reporting ('National Review Commission').
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off fetch for terminology and mandate; not a recurring collection target.
queries_used: Slovenia National Review Commission public procurement remedies decisions English annual report

candidates.source_name: Računsko sodišče RS – Arhiv revizij (Court of Audit audit archive)
candidates.why_relevant: Full-text audit reports of public-fund users. Audits of ministries, agencies and state-owned financial institutions routinely inspect procurement legality and payment/cash-management arrangements, naming banks, contract values and irregularities that never surfaced cleanly on the procurement portal. A confirmed example: the audit of SID banka operations found the Ministry of Finance had not ensured compliance with public procurement rules at the bank.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the audit archive listing, filter by auditee type and by keyword in report titles ('banka', 'plačilni promet', 'javno naročanje'); download and parse PDFs.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + snowball from result pages
queries_used: Računsko sodišče RS revizijsko poročilo javno naročilo banka plačilni promet
rs-rs.si revizijska poročila iskalnik javno naročanje Banka Slovenije revizija

candidates.source_name: Računsko sodišče RS – Seznam revidirancev (auditee index, incl. Banka Slovenije)
candidates.why_relevant: Entity-indexed view of every audit ever performed on a given body. The Banka Slovenije auditee page aggregates all audits of the central bank (e.g. supervisory-function audits); equivalent pages exist for SID banka, ministries and agencies. This is the fastest actor-first route into audit material relevant to banking and payments.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Build a watchlist of financial-sector auditee IDs and poll their pages for new audits.
queries_used: rs-rs.si revizijska poročila iskalnik javno naročanje Banka Slovenije revizija

candidates.source_name: Court of Audit of the Republic of Slovenia – English site and English audit reports
candidates.why_relevant: Selected audit reports and infographics published in English; lowers translation cost for the subset of audits that touch financial-sector procurement and state financial institutions.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl the English audit archive; treat as a partial mirror – always check the Slovenian archive for completeness.
queries_used: Slovenian Court of Audit English audit reports public procurement banking payment services

candidates.source_name: Računsko sodišče RS – Javna naročila (its own procurement publications)
candidates.why_relevant: The Court of Audit publishes its own contract awards, including the statutory annual list of below-EUR-40,000 contracts. Small but concrete: shows which suppliers (incl. payment/banking service providers) serve a control institution, and demonstrates the statutory 'seznam javnih naročil pod 40.000 EUR' obligation that applies to every Slovenian authority – a generalizable low-threshold disclosure vein.
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual fetch; generalize the pattern to other authorities' 'javne objave / javna naročila' subpages.
queries_used: Računsko sodišče RS revizijsko poročilo javno naročilo banka plačilni promet

candidates.source_name: KPK – Zaključne ugotovitve / odločitve komisije (final findings on concrete cases)
candidates.why_relevant: Published case findings of the anti-corruption commission, including cases on tenders allegedly tailored to a pre-selected bidder and breaches of procurement transparency. These name officials, authorities and often the favoured supplier – revealing contracts and relationships that procurement notices alone do not expose.
candidates.legal_status: official public-body publication; contains personal data – handle under GDPR minimisation
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl category pagination; keyword-filter for 'javno naročilo', 'banka', 'plačilni', 'kartic'; store findings text and the subject's response.
queries_used: KPK zaključne ugotovitve objave kpk-rs.si ugotovitve o konkretnem primeru javna naročila
KPK Komisija za preprečevanje korupcije ugotovitve javno naročilo finančne storitve banka

candidates.source_name: KPK – Analiza korupcijskih tveganj v postopkih javnega naročanja
candidates.why_relevant: Systemic KPK analysis of corruption risks in procurement procedures – gives the typology of manipulations (spec-tailoring, split contracts, single-bid awards) that an analyst should look for when reading award notices for bank/payment contracts, and often cites concrete case material.
candidates.access_status: open web PDF (a second copy exists under /kpk/wp-content/uploads/2020/02/analiza_-JN.pdf)
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off PDF download and parse; use as a red-flag taxonomy for scoring award notices.
queries_used: KPK zaključne ugotovitve objave kpk-rs.si ugotovitve o konkretnem primeru javna naročila

candidates.source_name: ERAR (KPK application: public-sector transaction records)
candidates.why_relevant: KPK-run database of actual money flows from public-sector bodies to legal and natural persons (10-year retention, relaunched 2024/2025). Lets an analyst see what a public body actually PAID a bank, card processor or POS/IT supplier – i.e. real contract execution value versus the awarded value, and supplier relationships never tendered. The most powerful indirect confirmation source in this cell.
candidates.access_status: open web application; bulk data also mirrored on OPSI
candidates.legal_status: statutory publication under ZIntPK arts. 75.a/75.b; personal-data transactions restricted by law – respect scope
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Prefer the OPSI dataset / any documented API over UI scraping; query by supplier tax ID (banks, processors) and by paying authority.
candidates.discovered_via_method: local-language search + snowball via KPK site
queries_used: Erar KPK aplikacija transakcije javnega sektorja banke plačila

candidates.source_name: KPK – Sporočila za javnost (press releases)
candidates.why_relevant: Earliest public signal that KPK has opened or closed a case; often summarises findings before the full document is posted, and flags systemic themes (e.g. procurement in state-owned financial institutions).
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Poll category listing weekly; RSS if exposed.
queries_used: KPK zaključne ugotovitve objave kpk-rs.si ugotovitve o konkretnem primeru javna naročila

candidates.source_name: KPK archive site (arhiv.kpk-rs.si)
candidates.why_relevant: Legacy KPK content (older findings, FAQs, guidance) that was not migrated to the current CMS. Necessary for historical depth on procurement cases predating the site redesign.
candidates.access_status: open web; legacy, may be partially broken
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off historical crawl; combine with Wayback Machine for gaps.

candidates.why_relevant: The policy directorate's own reports and analyses on the functioning of the Slovenian procurement system – market structure, competition levels, single-bid rates, CPV-level breakdowns. Provides the macro frame in which specific banking/payments tenders sit.

candidates.source_name: Sodna praksa RS – Iskalnik sodne prakse (case-law database, Upravno sodišče review of DKOM)
candidates.why_relevant: Since 1 January 2021 certain DKOM decisions can be challenged before the Administrative Court in Ljubljana. Those judgments (UPRS sodbe) restate the facts of the disputed tender – bidder names, specs, values – and give a second, independent narrative of the same procurement dispute, including cases where DKOM's decision was overturned.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Parameterised search harvesting with database=UPRS and Slovenian procurement keywords ('javno naročanje', 'zahtevek za revizijo', 'bančne storitve'); parse the jedro/institut metadata fields.

negative_findings.description: Neither the DKOM decisions listing nor the Court of Audit archive exposes a sector/CPV filter. The DKOM listing filters only by year and sorts by publication date, decision date or decision number; there is no 'bančne storitve' or CPV facet.
negative_findings.result_summary: Banking/payments decisions can only be isolated by full-text keyword search or by full-corpus crawl plus post-hoc classification.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design must assume full-corpus ingestion plus a Slovenian keyword classifier, not a cheap filtered feed. This drives volume and cost estimates.

negative_findings.description: A guessed URL https://www.dkom.si/sl/odlocitve-dkom/ returned HTTP 404. The working path is https://www.dkom.si/sl/revizijske-zadeve/odlocitve-dkom/ (decisions sit under the 'revizijske zadeve' section).
negative_findings.result_summary: 404 on a constructed path; correct path found via site navigation. Not evidence the site is down.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The site has been redesigned at least once; any stored URL set must be path-validated and legacy /odlocitve_DKOM/ links resolved, or collection will silently lose the historical corpus.

negative_findings.description: Slovenian and English searches for DKOM or KPK cases specifically about banking, card-processing or payment-system contracts returned no individual named case within this reconnaissance pass. Search engines surfaced institutional pages rather than case-level hits.
negative_findings.result_summary: The banking/payments subset of review and anti-corruption case law was not enumerated; only the containers holding it were identified.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that general web search is inadequate for case-level intelligence in this cell — retrieval must go through the institutions' own full-text search or a local index of the crawled corpus. This is a collection-design conclusion, not evidence that such cases do not exist.

negative_findings.description: DKOM's 'prekrškovne zadeve' section documents the misdemeanour procedure and sanctions but it was not established whether individual infringement decisions against contracting authorities are published as full documents or only described in aggregate.
negative_findings.result_summary: Procedure pages found; a case-level infringement register was not located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: If infringement decisions are not published individually, sanction-level intelligence would have to come from annual reports or FOI (ZDIJZ) requests instead.

negative_findings.description: No documented public API was found for DKOM decisions, the Court of Audit archive, or the KPK findings listing. ERAR is the only source in this cell with a machine-readable route confirmed by an open-data catalogue entry.
negative_findings.result_summary: HTML crawling appears to be the default access mode for three of the four core institutions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Sets engineering expectations: build resilient HTML parsers with change detection, and prefer OPSI datasets where they exist.

negative_findings.description: MJU's procurement directorate content exists across at least three hosts: the retired djn.mju.gov.si, the current ejn.gov.si, and gov.si asset paths. Older statistical reports are linked from the retired host.
negative_findings.result_summary: Multiple partially-overlapping hosts for the same institutional output.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Historical statistical series may be incomplete unless the retired host and Wayback snapshots are also harvested.

coverage_gaps.description: The banking/payments subset of DKOM decisions has not been enumerated — only the corpus containers were mapped.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a systematic pass through https://www.dkom.si/sl/iskalnik-po-odlocitvah-dkom/ with a Slovenian keyword set: bančne storitve, plačilni promet, plačilni sistem, POS terminal, kartično poslovanje, procesiranje kartic, bankomat, gotovinsko poslovanje, e-plačila, transakcijski račun, vodenje računov.

coverage_gaps.description: Sector regulators and specialised oversight bodies adjacent to this cell were not searched in this pass: Banka Slovenije (as supervisor and as a contracting authority), AJPES, Urad RS za preprečevanje pranja denarja, and the Fiskalni svet.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Extend the actor map to these bodies and check whether each publishes procurement decisions, supervisory findings or contract registers relevant to payments.

coverage_gaps.description: No freedom-of-information (ZDIJZ) route was assessed for material these bodies hold but do not publish — e.g. full bid documentation referenced in a DKOM decision.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Document the ZDIJZ request process and the Informacijski pooblaščenec (Information Commissioner) appeal route as a fallback acquisition channel, including its decisions database which itself adjudicates access to procurement documents.

coverage_gaps.description: Investigative media and civil-society watchdogs that translate DKOM/KPK/Court of Audit output into narrative (e.g. Oštro, Pod črto, Transparency International Slovenia, Necenzurirano) were not covered in this pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Scout the media/NGO layer as an indirect pointer tier — they often name parties and connect dots the official documents anonymise.

coverage_gaps.description: No verified crosswalk was established between DKOM decision numbers (018-nnn/YYYY), eNaročanje publication numbers (JN.../NMV...), TED notice IDs and ERAR supplier tax IDs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Design and test an entity-resolution layer keyed on contracting-authority name plus contract subject; DKOM prekrškovne files reportedly carry the portal publication number, which may be the strongest available join key.

coverage_gaps.description: Liveness, robots.txt policy, rate limits and terms of use were not checked for any domain in this slice — per instructions, URL verification is a separate deterministic pass.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run the liveness/robots verification pass over all listed domains before automating any crawl, paying particular attention to erar.si and sodnapraksa.si which are query-driven applications.

brief: Slovenia's procurement oversight layer is unusually well-consolidated and almost entirely open-web: DKOM (dkom.si) publishes every review decision back to the early 2000s with the contracting authority named in the URL and a dedicated full-text search engine, Računsko sodišče (rs-rs.si) publishes full audit reports indexed both chronologically and by auditee, KPK (kpk-rs.si) publishes case-level 'zaključne ugotovitve' plus the ERAR transaction database, and MJU/Direktorat za javno naročanje (ejn.gov.si, gov.si, mirrored on podatki.gov.si) publishes the statutory annual procurement statistics. The decisive limitation is retrieval rather than availability: none of the review or audit bodies offers a sector or CPV filter, and general web search does not reach case level, so isolating banking, card-processing and payment-system disputes requires full-corpus ingestion plus Slovenian-keyword classification, with sodnapraksa.si (UPRS judgments reviewing DKOM since 2021) as a valuable second narrative on the same disputes. ERAR is the strongest indirect confirmation source, showing what authorities actually paid banks and payment suppliers rather than what was awarded. Commercial aggregators (Tax-Fin-Lex, IUS-INFO) index this material usefully but are paywalled and should be used for discovery only, with authoritative copies pulled from the institutions themselves.
